materialFindings.title: Digital and Identity Fraud Risk: The organisation can detect identity misuse, account takeover or impersonation.
materialFindings.questionPrompt: The organisation can detect identity misuse, account takeover or impersonation.
materialFindings.methodologyVersionId: MFRS-V1.2-CANDIDATE-OWNER-CORRECTION
materialFindings.responseOperationalMeaning: Exists only informally or inconsistently.
materialFindings.responseMeaning: Initial / ad hoc: Exists only informally or inconsistently.
materialFindings.diagnosis: Identity misuse detection and investigation capability was self-assessed as "Initial / ad hoc" (Exists only informally or inconsistently; normalised score 20/100). This is self-reported and requires the listed operating evidence before it can be treated as verified.
materialFindings.whyItMatters: This recorded weakness affects a methodology hard gate and must be remediated before relying on the aggregate maturity result.
materialFindings.fraudMechanism: Identity misuse can continue when takeover, impersonation and unusual identity-bearing activity are not surfaced for timely challenge.
materialFindings.likelyFinancialImpact: Direct -- compromised or privileged access can alter records and transactions.
materialFindings.likelyOperationalImpact: Digital misuse can evade prevention and monitoring.
materialFindings.expectedControlStandard: Material identity-bearing systems and digital channels produce sufficient authentication, profile and activity signals to identify suspected identity misuse promptly.
evidenceToRequest: Log coverage inventory for identity-bearing systems
Defined retention period and data-protection basis
Investigation runbook and a worked case example
materialFindings.recommendedControl: Security Operations must monitor authentication, credential, profile, device and transaction signals across material identity-bearing systems, define takeover indicators and alert thresholds, and route suspected identity misuse into the separate investigation and containment process.
materialFindings.accountableOwner: Chief Technology Officer
materialFindings.operatingFrequency: Continuous logging and alerting; runbook exercised at least annually
minimumEvidenceCharacteristics: Covers authentication, profile change and transaction events together
Retention supports investigation within the defined window
Runbook includes containment actions
materialFindings.effectivenessMeasure: All material identity-bearing systems are logged with takeover alerting active and the runbook exercised annually.
materialFindings.escalationThreshold: A suspected takeover that cannot be reconstructed from logs, or a material system without identity logging.

materialFindings.title: Operational Fraud Controls: System and data access is granted against current role requirements.
materialFindings.questionPrompt: System and data access is granted against current role requirements.
materialFindings.methodologyVersionId: MFRS-V1.2-CANDIDATE-OWNER-CORRECTION
materialFindings.responseOperationalMeaning: Partially designed but not fully implemented.
materialFindings.responseMeaning: Partially designed: Partially designed but not fully implemented.
materialFindings.diagnosis: Role-based user-access governance was self-assessed as "Partially designed" (Partially designed but not fully implemented; normalised score 40/100). This is self-reported and requires the listed operating evidence before it can be treated as verified.
materialFindings.whyItMatters: This recorded weakness affects a methodology hard gate and must be remediated before relying on the aggregate maturity result.
materialFindings.fraudMechanism: Access granted without a current role basis can enable a person to initiate, approve or alter activity beyond legitimate responsibility.
materialFindings.likelyFinancialImpact: Direct -- access or supplier-control weakness can enable unauthorised payments or manipulation.
materialFindings.likelyOperationalImpact: Preventive controls may not match current roles or approved suppliers.

materialFindings.operatingFrequency: Quarterly and on every joiner, mover or leaver event

The role requirement is explicit
Incompatible access is identified and resolved or formally approved

contradictions.title: Operational and privileged-access weaknesses indicate one systemic access-governance issue
contradictions.drivingResponses: Digital and Identity Fraud Risk: Partially designed: Partially designed but not fully implemented; Operational Fraud Controls: Partially designed: Partially designed but not fully implemented
contradictions.whyItMatters: Excess access across ordinary and privileged environments can create an end-to-end manipulation and concealment route.
contradictions.falseComfortRisk: Treating the findings as unrelated domain issues understates the common identity and recertification dependency.
contradictions.whatLeadershipShouldVerify: Is one complete identity, role and recertification population used across ordinary and privileged access reviews?
contradictions.fraudPathwayEnabled: Excess access in one system is used to reach, execute or conceal activity in another.

contradictions.title: Operational Fraud Controls scores strongly but contains a failed critical control
contradictions.drivingResponses: Domain score 69/100; failed critical evidence: Operational Fraud Controls: Partially designed: Partially designed but not fully implemented.
contradictions.whyItMatters: A blended domain average can mask a control the methodology treats as non-negotiable.
contradictions.falseComfortRisk: Leadership may rely on the aggregate domain score and miss the exact failed control.
contradictions.whatLeadershipShouldVerify: Can current operating evidence independently demonstrate the control(s) covering Operational Fraud Controls?
contradictions.fraudPathwayEnabled: The specific failed control is exploited while the aggregate score discourages deeper review.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve accountable executive mandates and escalation authority for priority remediation.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 4 linked finding(s) and 3 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Hard-gate, governance and maturity-limiting controls require authority to allocate resources and resolve blockers.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Name one accountable executive per linked control and approve a 30-day escalation route.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Priority controls remain ownerless or blocked and the maturity reading remains constrained.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Signed mandate with decision rights, owners and escalation cadence.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Choose and record remediation rather than passive acceptance for Critical and High risks.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 4 linked finding(s) and 3 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Plausible consequence pathways require an explicit leadership treatment decision.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Approve linked treatments; any temporary acceptance must name an owner, expiry and compensating control.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Known risk pathways remain untreated without a documented acceptance basis.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Signed treatment decision for every Critical and High risk.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve the target control standards management will implement across the priority risk areas.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 8 linked finding(s) and 8 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Functions need one design baseline rather than independent interpretations of the findings.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Adopt the control-improvement register; deviations require documented oversight approval.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Partial or inconsistent designs fail to address the causal pathway.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Approved design baseline and named implementation owners.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve specialist capacity and resources for high-difficulty controls.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 4 linked finding(s) and 4 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: High-difficulty controls cannot meet target periods without committed capacity.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Fund the named supporting functions and require a resource-confirmed delivery plan.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: The highest-complexity gaps remain open despite nominal approval.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Resource plan showing accountable people, capacity and approved spend.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve prerequisite-first sequencing for dependent improvements.

leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Use authoritative roadmap dependency IDs and escalate threatened prerequisites.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Downstream controls are implemented on incomplete foundations.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Dependency-confirmed delivery sequence with escalation owners.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve a fixed fraud-risk implementation and control-effectiveness review cadence.

leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Require monthly implementation reporting and quarterly control-effectiveness review through the organisation’s management and oversight route.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "A suspected takeover that cannot be reconstructed from logs, or a material system without identity logging." and deliver the exact control design: Security Operations must monitor authentication, credential, profile, device and transaction signals across material identity-bearing systems, define takeover indicators and alert thresholds, and route suspected identity misuse into the separate investigation and containment process.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Technology Officer
roadmapActions.successMeasure: All material identity-bearing systems are logged with takeover alerting active and the runbook exercised annually.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Alert definitions for takeover indicators; Defined retention period and data-protection basis; Investigation runbook and a worked case example; Log coverage inventory for identity-bearing systems
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: A suspected takeover that cannot be reconstructed from logs, or a material system without identity logging.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Any missed quarterly review, unassigned account or removal overdue beyond 10 business days." and deliver the exact control design: System owners must maintain a current role-to-access matrix, require business-owner approval against the requester’s current duties before granting access, separate incompatible initiation and approval rights, and retain the request, approval and provisioning trail.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: COO
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% population reviewed quarterly and 95% of removal exceptions closed within 10 business days.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Access requests and approvals; Current role-to-access matrix; Provisioning audit trail; Segregation-of-duties exception decisions
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any missed quarterly review, unassigned account or removal overdue beyond 10 business days.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Any unknown or unjustified privileged account, missed recertification or leaver access beyond 24 hours." and deliver the exact control design: IT Security must maintain a complete sensitive-access inventory, require named identities and strong authentication, enforce least privilege and session logging, and remove access when the business justification ends; periodic recertification is handled by the separate access-review control.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Technology Officer
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% privileged accounts recertified quarterly; leaver access removed within 24 hours; zero unjustified shared admin accounts.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Approval and business justification; Privileged-account register; Privileged-session/access logs; Quarterly independent recertification; Removal tickets
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any unknown or unjustified privileged account, missed recertification or leaver access beyond 24 hours.
roadmapActions.dependency: System and data access is granted against current role requirements

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Activation before verification, an unapproved exception, or a sensitive change without re-verification." and deliver the exact control design: The process owner must define the risk points requiring verification, including customer or beneficiary enrolment, employee onboarding, supplier activation and counterparty contracting. Apply proportionate checks against independent sources such as identity documents validated for authenticity, company registration records and confirmation of contact details through independently obtained channels. Retain results and evidence under applicable data-protection obligations, require documented approval for exceptions, and trigger re-verification for sensitive profile or banking changes.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: COO / CFO
roadmapActions.processOwner: Process owners for onboarding and activation
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% of in-scope enrolments and activations carry completed verification before activation, with all exceptions approved.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Defined verification risk points and required checks; Exception approvals; re-verification records for sensitive changes; Verification records with source and date

essentialModel.conclusion: Fictional Owner-Managed Firm is not starting from zero. Its fraud leadership and governance and continuous improvement and fraud risk monitoring provide a useful foundation. The weakness is that these capabilities are not yet connected into a repeatable fraud-risk cycle, so ownership, challenge, detection and response do not yet reinforce one another. The next 90-day checkpoint should test whether ownership now operate as one system rather than as separate activities.
essentialModel.reportBasis: This report is based on management's responses to the MK Fraud Readiness assessment and MK's analytical methodology. It provides fraud-risk analysis and control-design guidance. MK has not independently tested whether controls operate in practice.

controls.controlDesign: Independently validate that "Fraud awareness is included in employee onboarding or induction" operates to the expected standard (Induction includes fraud content covering policy, reporting routes, consequences and role-relevant risks, is completed within a defined period of joining, and covers contractors where they hold equivalent access.) across the complete population, required frequency and under pressure. This does not assert a control defect; if validation identifies one, apply the recommended control design: The People lead must include a fraud module in induction covering the fraud policy and prohibited conduct, how and where to report, the protection from retaliation, the consequences of dishonest conduct, and the fraud risks specific to the joiner’s role; completion is required within a defined period of the start date, tracked against the joiner population from the HR system, extended to contractors with equivalent system or asset access, and overdue completion escalates to the hiring manager.
controls.accountableExecutiveRole: Chief People Officer
controls.operatingFrequency: On every joiner, within the defined completion period
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for on every joiner, within the defined completion period must be reconciled before sampling.
controls.effectivenessTest: At least 95% of joiners complete the fraud induction module within the defined period.
controls.escalationThreshold: Any joiner in a high-risk role granted access before completing induction fraud content.

scenarios.title: A compromised or impersonated identity is used to change a sensitive profile, instruction or transaction
scenarios.actorClass: An internal or external actor using an impersonated or insufficiently verified identity
scenarios.opportunity: Identity verification at material risk points is not yet applied consistently enough to prevent misuse.
scenarios.entryPoint: A customer, employee, supplier or counterparty is activated or materially changed without an independent verification step.
scenarios.mechanism: An actor presents an impersonated or manipulated identity to gain access, payment, credit, benefit or authority under another party’s name.
scenarios.concealment: The activity may appear routine until complete population review, independent approval or exception monitoring exposes it.
scenarios.consequence: Unauthorised access, payment, benefit or profile change can occur before the identity or transaction is challenged. compromised or privileged access can alter records and transactions. Digital misuse can evade prevention and monitoring.
warningIndicators: Activation before verification, an unapproved exception, or a sensitive change without re-verification.
An exception, access, approval or incident record that cannot be reconciled to the complete in-scope population.
Credential reset, device change or profile amendment
Identity data differs across trusted records
Sensitive transaction follows a new or unusual session
scenarios.controlWeakness: Identity verification and sensitive-change monitoring are partially designed.
scenarios.interruptionPoint: Security Operations must monitor authentication, credential, profile, device and transaction signals across material identity-bearing systems, define takeover indicators and alert thresholds, and route suspected identity misuse into the separate investigation and containment process.; The process owner must define the risk points requiring verification, including customer or beneficiary enrolment, employee onboarding, supplier activation and counterparty contracting. Apply proportionate checks against independent sources such as identity documents validated for authenticity, company registration records and confirmation of contact details through independently obtained channels. Retain results and evidence under applicable data-protection obligations, require documented approval for exceptions, and trigger re-verification for sensitive profile or banking changes.
scenarios.immediateContainment: Pause the sensitive change or transaction, re-perform identity verification through a trusted route and preserve authentication records.
scenarios.longTermResponse: Implement risk-based identity verification, profile-change controls, authentication evidence and takeover investigation.

scenarios.title: Privileged access is used to alter a value-bearing record, entitlement or audit trail
scenarios.actorClass: An internal or external actor using privileged or excessive digital access
scenarios.opportunity: Sensitive access is not yet restricted and reviewed consistently enough to prevent or quickly challenge misuse.
scenarios.entryPoint: A privileged, administrative or emergency-access account remains usable without independent periodic review.
scenarios.mechanism: An actor uses privileged access to alter a record, entitlement or transaction and relies on weak recertification or monitoring to avoid timely challenge.
scenarios.concealment: The activity may appear routine until complete population review, independent approval or exception monitoring exposes it.
scenarios.consequence: Unauthorised changes to a value-bearing record, entitlement or audit trail can create loss and weaken investigation. compromised or privileged access can alter records and transactions. Digital misuse can evade prevention and monitoring.
warningIndicators: An exception, access, approval or incident record that cannot be reconciled to the complete in-scope population.
Missed review, unknown access or removal overdue beyond the defined service level.
Emergency or administrator access outside the role pattern
Unusual record or entitlement change
Access review exception remains overdue
scenarios.controlWeakness: Privileged access is not consistently restricted, logged and independently recertified.
scenarios.interruptionPoint: IT Security must maintain a complete sensitive-access inventory, require named identities and strong authentication, enforce least privilege and session logging, and remove access when the business justification ends; periodic recertification is handled by the separate access-review control.; IT Security must reconcile the complete sensitive-access and administrator population to current owners and role requirements at least quarterly, obtain an independent keep/remove decision from system owners, record exceptions and close removals within the defined service level; emergency and service accounts are included.; System owners must export the complete active-user access population on a defined cycle, obtain business-owner keep/remove decisions against current responsibilities, route exceptions to IT for closure and reconcile leaver and mover removals to the HR feed.
scenarios.immediateContainment: Suspend or restrict the affected entitlement, preserve access and audit logs, and route the change for accountable review.
scenarios.longTermResponse: Implement role-based access, privileged-session logging, periodic recertification and exception escalation.

materialFindings.title: A payment instruction received by email is acted on
materialFindings.questionPrompt: Is there an organisation-wide rule that payment details, salary details or urgent payment requests received by email are never acted on without confirmation through a separate, known channel?
materialFindings.methodologyVersionId: Review bank 1.3 (draft, not approved by MK)
materialFindings.responseLabel: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.
materialFindings.responseOperationalMeaning: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.
materialFindings.responseMeaning: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.
materialFindings.diagnosis: 1 of the 1 control answered for this scheme was reported as a gap. Payment changes received by email are acted on as received. Reported by the respondent; not independently tested.
materialFindings.whyItMatters: Acting on payment instructions received by email is how business email compromise succeeds.
materialFindings.fraudMechanism: Changed details or urgent payments are processed on the strength of an email. The method links it to business email compromise and payment redirection and takeover of staff accounts.
materialFindings.likelyFinancialImpact: Payments, credit or goods released to someone impersonating a supplier, customer, employee or executive.
materialFindings.likelyOperationalImpact: Accounts and instructions would need to be revalidated and affected parties contacted.
materialFindings.expectedControlStandard: An organisation-wide rule requires confirmation through a separate, known channel for every payment, salary or urgent request received by email, and staff follow it.
evidenceToRequest: The written rule, staff communication, call-back records for a sample of requests.
materialFindings.recommendedControl: An organisation-wide rule requires confirmation through a separate, known channel for every payment, salary or urgent request received by email, and staff follow it.
materialFindings.accountableOwner: Head of IT or IT provider
materialFindings.processOwner: Head of IT or IT provider

materialFindings.effectivenessMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: an organisation-wide rule requires confirmation through a separate, known channel for every payment, salary or urgent request received by email, and staff follow it.
materialFindings.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where a payment instruction received by email is acted on, or any case processed without this control: email never enough on its own.

materialFindings.questionPrompt: Is there an agreed way to verify a request made by phone, voice note or video, such as calling back on a known number or using a code word, that applies to everyone including executives?
materialFindings.methodologyVersionId: Review bank 1.3 (draft, not approved by MK)
materialFindings.responseLabel: Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement.
materialFindings.responseOperationalMeaning: Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement.
materialFindings.responseMeaning: Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement.: Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement.
materialFindings.diagnosis: 4 of the 4 controls answered for this scheme were reported as gaps. Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement. Pressure triggers verification: only in some areas, cases or periods. Most changes are verified through the old details or another trusted route. Gift cards and PIN requests banned: only in some areas, cases or periods. Reported by the respondent and Finance; not independently tested.
materialFindings.whyItMatters: Voices and faces can be cloned, so only an agreed verification method holds.
materialFindings.fraudMechanism: A caller who sounds or looks like a known person is believed. The method links it to deepfake voice and video impersonation of executives and staff, business email compromise and payment redirection, takeover of staff accounts and SIM swaps and intercepted one-time PINs.
materialFindings.likelyFinancialImpact: Payments, credit or goods released to someone impersonating a supplier, customer, employee or executive.
materialFindings.likelyOperationalImpact: Accounts and instructions would need to be revalidated and affected parties contacted.
materialFindings.expectedControlStandard: An agreed method, such as a call-back on a known number or a code word, applies to everyone, including executives, and staff know they are expected to use it.
evidenceToRequest: The verification procedure, briefing records for executives, simulation results.

essentialModel.conclusion: Fictional Owner-Managed Firm is not starting from zero: 36 schemes have every control that stops them reported in place. The work is concentrated. 4 first-priority schemes, most of them in digital and identity, need the specific controls named in this report, owned by the people the method names for them. Management should also not rely on the control reported in place whose own practices were reported as gaps until its owner confirms how it works.
essentialModel.reportBasis: This report is based on the organisation's own answers to the MK Fraud Readiness review, given by the respondent and the accountable functions named in it, and read against the draft review method, which MK has not yet approved. MK has not independently tested whether controls operate in practice, and no evidence was reviewed; evidence review is a separate Advisory service. findings.assessedPosition: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.
findings.assessedDiagnosis: 1 of the 1 control answered for this scheme was reported as a gap. Payment changes received by email are acted on as received. Reported by the respondent; not independently tested.
findings.fraudMechanism: Changed details or urgent payments are processed on the strength of an email. The method links it to business email compromise and payment redirection and takeover of staff accounts.
findings.whyItMatters: Acting on payment instructions received by email is how business email compromise succeeds.

findings.assessedPosition: Email accounts are protected by passwords only.
findings.assessedDiagnosis: 1 of the 1 control answered for this scheme was reported as a gap. Email accounts are protected by passwords only. Reported by the respondent; not independently tested.
findings.fraudMechanism: A mailbox without strong sign-in is used to send or intercept payment instructions. The method links it to takeover of staff accounts, business email compromise and payment redirection, spoofed or lookalike email in the organisation's name, criminals impersonating the organisation to customers, suppliers and the public and slow response that lets losses grow.
findings.whyItMatters: Most business email compromise starts with an account that has no multi-factor authentication.

findings.assessedPosition: Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement.
findings.assessedDiagnosis: 4 of the 4 controls answered for this scheme were reported as gaps. Some staff check unusual requests, depending on their own judgement. Pressure triggers verification: only in some areas, cases or periods. Most changes are verified through the old details or another trusted route. Gift cards and PIN requests banned: only in some areas, cases or periods. Reported by the respondent and Finance; not independently tested.
findings.fraudMechanism: A caller who sounds or looks like a known person is believed. The method links it to deepfake voice and video impersonation of executives and staff, business email compromise and payment redirection, takeover of staff accounts and SIM swaps and intercepted one-time PINs.
findings.whyItMatters: Voices and faces can be cloned, so only an agreed verification method holds.

scenarios.title: A payment instruction received by email is acted on
scenarios.actorClass: An insider, supplier or outsider who finds the step unguarded
scenarios.opportunity: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.
scenarios.entryPoint: Changed details or urgent payments are processed on the strength of an email.
scenarios.mechanism: Acting on payment instructions received by email is how business email compromise succeeds. What the answers show: Payment changes received by email are acted on as received.
scenarios.concealment: Without email never enough on its own, the activity is processed as routine and nothing records the exception.
scenarios.consequence: Payments, credit or goods released to someone impersonating a supplier, customer, employee or executive. Accounts and instructions would need to be revalidated and affected parties contacted.
warningIndicators: Business email compromise and payment redirection
